```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
```

```{r}
#| cache: true
groups <- read_parquet("data/groups.parquet")
market_groups <- read_parquet("data/market_groups.parquet")

markets <- read_parquet("data/markets.parquet")
history <- open_dataset("data/history.parquet")

joined <- history |>
  left_join(markets |> select(market_id, outcome, resolved_at), by = "market_id") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    outcome_numeric = case_when(
      outcome == "YES" ~ 1,
      outcome == "NO" ~ 0
    ),
    absolute_error = abs(probability - outcome_numeric),
    days_to_resolution = as.integer(as.Date(resolved_at) - date),
    time_bucket = case_when(
      days_to_resolution == 0 ~ "Final day",
      days_to_resolution <= 7 ~ "1 to 7 days",
      days_to_resolution <= 30 ~ "7 to 30 days",
      days_to_resolution <= 90 ~ "30 to 90 days",
      days_to_resolution > 90 ~ "More than 90 days"
    ),
    time_bucket = factor(
      time_bucket,
      levels = c(
        "Final day",
        "1 to 7 days",
        "7 to 30 days",
        "30 to 90 days",
        "More than 90 days"
      ),
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )
```

```{r}
accuracy <- joined |>
  group_by(time_bucket) |>
  summarise(
    mean_prediction_error = mean(absolute_error),
    snapshots = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(accuracy)

ggplot(accuracy, aes(x = time_bucket, y = mean_prediction_error, group = 1)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Prediction markets get smarter near the deadline",
    subtitle = "Mean absolute error in Manifold Markets forecasts, by days remaining",
    x = "Time until resolution",
    y = "Mean absolute error"
  )
```

```{r}
final_day <- joined |>
  filter(days_to_resolution == 0)

ggplot(final_day, aes(x = probability)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(
    x = "Forecast probability",
    y = "Number of snapshots"
  )
```

```{r}
calibration <- final_day |>
  mutate(
    probability_bin = cut(
      probability,
      breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
      include.lowest = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(probability_bin) |>
  summarise(
    predicted_probability = mean(probability),
    actual_rate = mean(outcome_numeric),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(calibration)

ggplot(calibration, aes(x = predicted_probability, y = actual_rate)) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(size = n)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Final-day forecasts track observed YES rates",
    x = "Mean predicted probability",
    y = "Actual YES rate",
    size = "Markets"
  )
```

`market_groups` links markets to topics through `market_id`; its `group_slug` links
to the corresponding topic details in `groups`. Since each market can have multiple
group slugs, `market_groups` is the many-to-many link table between `markets` and `groups`.
